final_answer:
The nonexpansiveness condition on each step forces
\[
0\le \alpha,\beta\le \frac14,
\]
because \(|1-\gamma\lambda|\le 1\) for all \(\lambda\in[1,8]\) is equivalent to \(0\le \gamma\lambda\le 2\), hence \(0\le\gamma\le 1/4\).

Let
\[
p(\lambda)=(1-\alpha\lambda)(1-\beta\lambda).
\]
If either step size is \(0\), then \(p(1)\ge 3/4\), so such a pair cannot be optimal once we find a value below that. Thus write
\[
r=\frac1\alpha,\qquad q=\frac1\beta,
\]
with \(4\le r\le q\). Then
\[
p(\lambda)=\frac{(r-\lambda)(q-\lambda)}{rq}.
\]

On \([1,2]\), both factors are positive and decreasing, so the maximum there occurs at \(\lambda=1\):
\[
p(1)=\frac{(r-1)(q-1)}{rq}.
\]

Suppose \(\rho\le 3/5\). Then in particular
\[
\frac{(r-1)(q-1)}{rq}\le \frac35.
\]
Writing \(S=r+q,\ T=rq\), this gives
\[
5(T-S+1)\le 3T
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T\le \frac{5S-5}{2}.
\]
Also, since \(r,q\ge4\),
\[
(r-4)(q-4)\ge0
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T\ge 4S-16.
\]
Combining,
\[
4S-16\le \frac{5S-5}{2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
S\le 9.
\]

If \(q\ge 8\), then already \(p(1)>3/5\), so we must have \(q<8\). Hence \(p(8)\ge0\), and \(\rho\le3/5\) also gives
\[
\frac{(8-r)(8-q)}{rq}\le \frac35.
\]
That is
\[
5(64-8S+T)\le 3T
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
T\le 20S-160.
\]
Together with \(T\ge4S-16\), this yields
\[
4S-16\le 20S-160
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
S\ge 9.
\]
Thus \(S=9\). Then the previous inequalities force
\[
T=20.
\]
So \(r,q\) are the roots of
\[
x^2-9x+20=0,
\]
hence
\[
\{r,q\}=\{4,5\}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\{\alpha,\beta\}=\left\{\frac14,\frac15\right\}.
\]

For this pair,
\[
p(\lambda)=\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{4}\right)\left(1-\frac{\lambda}{5}\right).
\]
On \([1,2]\), the maximum is
\[
p(1)=\frac34\cdot\frac45=\frac35.
\]
On \([4,8]\), the endpoint values are \(p(4)=0\), \(p(8)=3/5\), and the interior minimum occurs at \(\lambda=9/2\), where \(p(9/2)=-1/80\). Thus \(|p(\lambda)|\le 3/5\) on \([4,8]\).

So the minimum possible value is
\[
\boxed{\frac35},
\]
and the unique optimizing unordered pair is
\[
\boxed{\left\{\alpha,\beta\right\}=\left\{\frac14,\frac15\right\}}.
\]
